newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-RBA cautious on more rate cuts - Access.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-RBA cautious on more rate cuts - Access.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of Australia will probably be cautious about further interest rate cuts because of wages worries, Access Economics said in a report.
The report was written before Wednesday's 0.5 percentage point monetary easing but assumed a cut before Christmas.

Access said the bank would be cautious about subsequent rate cuts with enterprise bargains producing five percent annual wage rises and the Australian Council of Trade Unions calling for higher award wages.
"If the economy showed signs of stalling rates would be cut again," Access said.
The economy was weaker than the budget forecast and unemployment would edge up towards nine percent in mid-1997, the consultancy forecast.
Australia's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate stood at 8.7 percent in September.
The government forecasts 8.25 percent unemployment in the June quarter of 1997.

Access said: "However, if housing picks up in 1997 as expected, business investment -- led by communications and resources -- keeps rising and manufacturing stocks are run down, the economy can swing up without the need for major
If unemployment rises as expected the bank would be under extreme pressure to cut rates a third time in the current round.
The bank dropped its overnight cash rate target on Wednesday to 6.5 percent from 7.0 percent.
The previous cut, in July, had been the first since 1993.
